I1.quote: Hydrogen adsorption capacity at 77 K under the pressure range of 0–800 mmHg was determined by a volumetric method using the Micromeritics ASAP 2020HD88 system.
I1.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 3298), Section 2 Material and methods

I2.quote: The nitrogen doping concentration, specific surface area, and total pore volume of the N-doped CNTs were determined to be 1.5 at%, 135 m2/g, and 0.38 cm3/g, respectively.

I3.quote: The hydrogen adsorption measurements at 77 K showed that the N-doped CNTs exhibits gravimetric hydrogen uptake of 0.21 wt% at 1 bar and 1.21 wt% at 7 bar.

I4.quote: Based on the N2 sorption data, the BET surface area and total pore volume for the prepared N-doped CNTs are determined to be 135 m2/g and 0.38 cm3/g, respectively.
I4.location: main, p. 5 (journal p. 3301), Section 3 Results and discussion

I5.quote: This paper reports a facile method for the preparation of nitrogen-doped carbon nanotubes (N-doped CNTs) that shows enhanced hydrogen storage capacity.

notes: Single sorbent: N-doped bamboo-like CNTs from FeCl3-catalysed melamine pyrolysis; N/C atomic ratio ~0.015 (XPS 1.5 at%), so carbon is the majority component; paper notes 'the small amount of iron residue' (main p. 6, Section 3) after HCl washing, no Fe content given. H2 uptake measured volumetrically (ASAP 2020, 77 K, 0-800 mmHg, Fig. 5a) and gravimetrically (Hiden IGA, 77 K and 298 K, 0-19 bar, Fig. 5b,c; reported as excess). Table 1 values for other materials are quoted from refs [8],[11],[13],[20], not this paper's measurements. No retraction notice; record is_retracted false. No statement of prior publication of the data. No supplementary files supplied.
